response.text:
(p. 100)
This is a very interesting idea, and I think it has a lot of potential. If we can get past the idea that there is some antecedent fact that the practice is tracking, then it seems that we can make sense of the idea that the practice itself is the criterion of identity over time. This would mean that the criterion of identity over time is not a fact about the world, but a fact about our practice of ascription. This would have important implications for how we think about personal identity and how we hold each other accountable for our actions.
